tour.name: Peru Highlights 8-Day Private Tour: Lima, the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu & Cusco
tour.subtitle: Eight days from the coast to the Andes with private guides: Lima's colonial centre and ceviche, the Sacred Valley's Inca terraces and weavers, the train to Machu Picchu with a night at its foot, and the Inca and colonial capital of Cusco, with Moray and the Maras salt pans.

tour.overview:
Peru's great journey leads from the Pacific coast to the heart of the Inca Empire. This private tour begins in Lima, the colonial capital and the gastronomic capital of South America, then flies to Cusco and descends straight to the lower Sacred Valley to acclimatise gently. From Ollantaytambo the train follows the Urubamba to Machu Picchu, where a night at the foot of the mountain allows two visits, and the trip ends in Cusco, the Inca capital.

You have private guides and cars throughout, a domestic flight, the Vistadome train, timed tickets for Machu Picchu and seven nights in well-located hotels with breakfast. The itinerary is designed around altitude, going up gradually from the valley to Cusco.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 8 days, 7 nights
• Start: Lima Jorge Chávez Airport or your hotel in Lima
• End: Cusco airport or your hotel in Cusco
• Type: private tour with licensed guides, private cars, domestic flight and train; 7 nights with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, hotels, trains, Machu Picchu tickets and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; altitude from sea level to 3,400 metres

WHAT YOU SEE
• Lima: the colonial centre, San Francisco and Barranco.
• The Sacred Valley: Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero, Moray and Maras.
• Machu Picchu, twice.
• Cusco: the cathedral, Qorikancha, San Blas and Sacsayhuamán.

WHY THIS WORKS
Starting in the valley at 2,800 metres and ending in Cusco at 3,400 metres helps your body adjust, and a night in Aguas Calientes means you can see Machu Picchu in the quiet of early morning.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Peru, couples, families and small groups.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want more, add Lake Titicaca, Arequipa and the Colca Canyon, or the Amazon.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Machu Picchu tickets and trains sell out early, especially from May to September: book as early as possible. Bring your passport for all tickets.

days.name: Arrival in Lima and an evening in Barranco
days.description:
What to expect: a private welcome and a first taste of Peru.

Your driver meets you at Jorge Chávez Airport and drives you to your hotel in Miraflores. In the evening your guide takes you to Barranco for a walk and dinner suggestions in one of the world's great food cities.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Any time – Airport transfer.
18:00 – Evening walk in Barranco.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Lima traffic is heavy; allow time.

INCLUDED: airport transfer, evening walk.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in Miraflores.
Meals: none.

days.name: Lima: the colonial centre and a ceviche lunch, then fly to Cusco and the Sacred Valley
days.description:
What to expect: Lima's history and food, then the Andes.

In the morning you visit the Plaza Mayor, the cathedral and the monastery of San Francisco with its catacombs, and have a ceviche lunch. In the afternoon you fly to Cusco, about 1 hour 20 minutes, where your driver takes you straight down to your hotel in the Sacred Valley, lower and gentler for your first nights at altitude.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Colonial Lima.
12:30 – Ceviche lunch.
15:00 – Flight to Cusco.
17:30 – Drive to the Sacred Valley.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Rest this evening and drink coca tea.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, guide, tickets, lunch, flight, transfers.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in the Sacred Valley.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: The Sacred Valley: Pisac, Chinchero and the weavers
days.description:
What to expect: Inca terraces and Andean culture.

You visit the citadel of Pisac and its market, have lunch in the valley and meet the weavers of Chinchero, who show you natural dyeing and weaving.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Pisac.
13:00 – Lunch.
15:00 – Chinchero.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Walk slowly on the terraces.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, guide, tourist ticket, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in the Sacred Valley.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Ollantaytambo, the train to Aguas Calientes and an afternoon at Machu Picchu
days.description:
What to expect: the fortress-temple of Ollantaytambo and a first visit to Machu Picchu.

You explore Ollantaytambo and its Inca town in the morning, then board the Vistadome train to Aguas Calientes. In the afternoon, your guide takes you up to Machu Picchu for a first visit, when the light is soft and the morning crowds have left. You spend the night at the foot of the mountain.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Ollantaytambo.
11:30 – Train to Aguas Calientes.
14:00 – Machu Picchu, first visit.
17:00 – Back in Aguas Calientes.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring only a small overnight bag; your main luggage goes to Cusco.

INCLUDED: transfers, train, bus, entry, guide, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in Aguas Calientes.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

stops.name: Machu Picchu
stops.description: A first visit in the afternoon light.

days.name: Machu Picchu at dawn and the train back to Cusco
days.description:
What to expect: Machu Picchu in the quiet of the morning.

You take an early bus up for a second visit on another circuit, often with mist lifting from the peaks, with time to explore at your own pace or climb Huayna Picchu if you have booked it. After lunch in Aguas Calientes, you take the train back to Ollantaytambo and drive to your hotel in Cusco.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:00 – Bus to Machu Picchu.
06:30 – Second visit.
11:30 – Lunch in Aguas Calientes.
14:30 – Train to Ollantaytambo.
18:00 – Arrival in Cusco.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Huayna Picchu tickets are limited and must be booked early.

INCLUDED: bus, entry, guide, lunch, train, transfers.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in Cusco.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Cusco: the cathedral, Qorikancha, San Blas and Sacsayhuamán
days.description:
What to expect: the Inca capital and its colonial heart.

You visit the Plaza de Armas and the cathedral, walk past the twelve-angled stone to San Blas, see the Temple of the Sun at Qorikancha, have lunch, and drive up to the giant walls of Sacsayhuamán.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Cathedral.
11:00 – San Blas and Qorikancha.
13:00 – Lunch.
15:00 – Sacsayhuamán.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Cusco is at 3,400 metres; walk slowly.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, guide, tickets, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in Cusco.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Moray and the Maras salt pans, and a free afternoon in Cusco
days.description:
What to expect: the plateau above the Sacred Valley.

You visit the circular terraces of Moray and the salt pans of Maras in the morning, and return to Cusco for lunch and a free afternoon to explore markets and museums.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Drive to Moray.
09:15 – Moray.
11:15 – Maras salt pans.
13:30 – Lunch in Cusco.
Afternoon – Free.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A farewell dinner with a folk music show can be arranged.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, guide, tickets, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: hotel in Cusco.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Departure from Cusco
days.description:
What to expect: a private transfer to the airport.

After breakfast, your driver takes you to Cusco airport for your onward flight, usually via Lima.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
As needed – Private transfer to the airport.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Extensions to Lake Titicaca or the Amazon can be added.

INCLUDED: airport transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

stops.description: A last coffee on the Plaza de Armas.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels, trains, Machu Picchu tickets and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the flight to Cusco included?
faq.answer: Yes, Lima to Cusco in economy with a checked bag.

faq.question: How do you handle the altitude?
faq.answer: The trip starts in the Sacred Valley at 2,800 metres and ends in Cusco at 3,400 metres, giving your body time to adjust. Drink water and coca tea and take it slowly.

faq.question: Why two visits to Machu Picchu?
faq.answer: Entry is by timed circuits; two visits let you see more of the site and experience it in both afternoon and early-morning light.

faq.question: Can we hike the Inca Trail?
faq.answer: Yes, on a longer trip: the classic four-day trail requires permits booked months ahead; a one-day Inca Trail can replace the afternoon visit.

faq.question: What kind of hotels are used?
faq.answer: Comfortable 4-star or boutique hotels; upgrades to luxury lodges in the Sacred Valley and at Machu Picchu are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who cope with altitude and walking. We can book family rooms.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Inca sites have many steps; tell us your needs and we will adapt.

faq.question: Can we add Lake Titicaca?
faq.answer: Yes. Two nights in Puno with the Uros and Taquile islands fit well after Cusco.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers for cold mornings and warm days, a rain jacket, sun protection and good walking shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October is dry. November to March is rainy but green and quieter.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 30 days before the tour starts; trains, flights and Machu Picchu tickets are non-refundable once issued. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
